Subject: Re: Kubernetes on-prem deployment — site constraints & next steps

Alex — thanks for the inventory and the clear list. Below are concise recommendations to get the pilot scoped; we can expand items during the preflight call.

1) Cluster footprint (pilot -> prod):
- Control plane: 3 control-plane VMs (or nodes) on metal or isolated VMs, 8 vCPU / 32GB RAM each; tainted with control-plane:k=true. Keep etcd on those control plane nodes with local SSD or mirrored blockstore.
- Infra nodes (kube-system services): 3 x 8v/32GB for logging/monitoring, or run as smaller VMs if you prefer consolidation.
- Inference node pool(s): start with 4 x GPU worker nodes for pilot (NVIDIA A10/A100 depending on availability): 1-2 GPUs per node, 64–128GB RAM, 16–32 vCPU. Scale plan: add GPU nodes in groups of 4 to meet throughput.

2) Storage pattern:
- Model artifacts: central encrypted blockstore (Ceph/Rook or cloud-equivalent iSCSI) with a DynamicProvisioner (storageclass redwood-block-encrypted). Models are large but read-mostly; provision a dedicated PV class with 3x replication or erasure coding depending on the storage back-end.
- KV / prefix cache: use local NVMe on worker nodes for LRU cache (kv-cache directory on local SSD) — significantly reduces network overhead and latency. Ephemeral cache can be mounted via emptyDir backed by local SSD.
- Checkpoints/logs: use an object store (S3-compatible) for durability; write-ahead logs and audit logs go to central object store with lifecycle policies.

3) Networking & egress:
- Control plane: private control plane requires outbound to Redwood control-plane endpoints (we'll give FQDNs/CIDRs). Allow egress TCP/443 to those endpoints and to our update mirrors for images.
- Node pull frequency: models are pulled during deploys or cache misses — expect occasional large downloads (GBs) during model installs. If you want to avoid large external pulls, we can mirror images/models to an internal registry/edge cache.
- Required ports: kube-apiserver ports (6443) between control plane and agents; node-to-control-plane health checks; metrics/monitoring ports we will document in the preflight.

4) Compliance / evidence:
- For SOC2 preflight: collect KMS config (customer KMS ARNs), audit log retention policy, network architecture diagram, and proof of encryption at rest for blockstore. We will provide a checklist in the draft runbook.

Next steps:
- Can you send IOPS/IO size expectations for model loads and typical inference QPS? That will let us size NVMe cache and blockstore IO tiers.
- I'm looping in our networking and ops leads internally to prepare ACLs and a draft runbook (attached).

Proposed meeting times: Tue 2026-11-02 09:00 MDT or Wed 2026-11-03 10:00 MDT — let me know which works.

Regards,

Olga — draft sizing attached (node-sizing-table.xlsx) and a short summary below. I've kept two options as requested: conservative (pilot-focused) and aggressive (production scale).

Conservative (pilot):
- 3 control-plane nodes: 8vCPU / 32GB, 1 x 240GB SSD for etcd backups.
- 3 infra nodes: 8vCPU / 32GB, for logging/monitoring/storage control-plane (can be medium VMs).
- 4 GPU workers (A10 equivalent): each with 2 GPUs, 64GB RAM, 24 vCPU, 2 x 1TB NVMe (one for KV cache, one for ephemeral IO).
Estimated baseline throughput: ~6k tokens/sec (batching 8, model latent ~70ms).

Aggressive (initial prod):
- Keep control-plane/infras as above.
- 12 GPU workers in 3x groups of 4: each node as above. Adds headroom for model variants and canary testing.
IO configuration notes:
- Local NVMe for cache: mount at /var/lib/redwood/cache, use ext4 with noatime. Provide 1TB per GPU node as the default; increase if models are very large or you plan to cache multiple large models.
- Central blockstore: recommend a replicated blockstore with 20k IOPS baseline if you expect frequent model pulls; otherwise schedule model pre-population to avoid peak pulls.

I've flagged two network asks in the attached network-acl-draft.txt: outbound registry mirror (TCP/443), control plane endpoints (list), and a preference for customer NAT with source IP allowlisting.

I'll be on the call Tue 11/02 09:00 MDT.

-Jonas
